title: cf-unit-cell — the atom of a unit chart, where absence is drawn as no ink

findings.method: checked = the 20 contrast pairs in the payload's three measurement tables, each computed from design-system/tokens/tokens.json release 0.2.0 by resolving the alias chain to a hex and applying WCAG relative luminance (Y = 0.2126R + 0.7152G + 0.0722B on linearised sRGB), ratio = (Yl + 0.05) / (Yd + 0.05). All 20 are re-derived on demand by verify-contrast.py in this directory, which fails if any printed figure disagrees by more than 0.002. found = 5 properties of release 0.2.0 that constrain the design and that no document stated before this one: (1) adjacent ordinal steps in a single-hue ramp do NOT clear the 3:1 SC 1.4.11 floor — teal.60/teal.70 is 1.545:1 and teal.70/teal.90 is 1.958:1 — so the spacing.01 gutter is load-bearing rather than cosmetic and an ungutted grid fails AA; (2) semantic.focus (blue.60) measures 1.003:1 against palette.teal.60 because both sit at Y approx 0.160 on the universal ladder, so a single-colour focus ring is invisible on the lightest ordinal fill and the two-tone semantic.focus + semantic.focus-inset pair is mandatory, not decorative; (3) semantic.border.subtle-01 is 1.446:1 on palette.bone.default and cannot carry any border that carries meaning — which also affects cf-card and cf-table, both of which declare it as their only border token; (4) release 0.2.0 has no border-width axis and no px-denominated dimension token, so a border width is expressible only by using spacing.01 off-label and no token can guarantee a CSS-px target size for SC 2.5.8; (5) cf-chart-palette cannot express an ordinal ramp — four of its five series (blue.60 4.234:1, purple.60 4.235:1, magenta.60 4.239:1, teal.60 4.223:1) are luminance-identical against the ground and the fifth, cyan.40, is 2.003:1 and misses the 3:1 non-text floor, while its tokens_used carries one step per hue so the sequential and diverging variants it advertises have no values behind them. skipped = 4 checks not run and claimed in neither direction: no render was produced, so the dashed prior-art border at a 12px cell is a judgement (payload assumption A-3) and not a measurement; no screen-reader pass; no forced-colors render; no 400% zoom or 320px reflow of a 770-cell grid. Skipped is not passed.

notes.this_is_a_proposal: Nothing here is in design-system/component-index.json and this artifact did not write to it. Promotion is explicit human approval recorded as an ADR (CLAUDE.md, 'The membrane') and screen-producer cannot perform it. Until an ADR exists, <CfUnitCell> is a Gate B blocker and that is the correct behaviour.
notes.why_a_new_workstream: design-system-authoring did not exist. The four that did are brand-foundations (the brand, its tokens and their contrast), design-system-selection (which vendor design system to adopt), luma-travel (a client research and dashboard thread) and system-operations (the operating cost of the agent apparatus). This artifact is a proposal to enter component-index.json: it outlives the Luma board it was prompted by, it is not procurement, it is not the brand, and it is not cost. Filing it under luma-travel would put a design-system proposal inside a client thread and make the membrane harder to audit. The directory is new; nothing else was changed to accommodate it. Same reasoning ART-010 recorded when it created system-operations.
notes.level_1_is_a_load_bearing_choice: Proposed at level 1, and not only because ADR-012's test is 'derivable from tokens alone'. validation/adapters/carbon-react.py line 323 preserves entries where level == 1 and rebuilds everything else from the Carbon tarball, and lines 372-375 unconditionally delete every .json in design-system/components/. A CoForge-authored LEVEL 2 entry would therefore be erased on the next `--apply` run, and audit-contracts.py check 4d would then report it as a parity error. Level 2 is currently a lossy destination for anything CoForge authors. Reported in validation.md as a finding against the repository, not worked around here.
